fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled MMR-encoded gray-scale data (1 byte, 0x37, in the PoC) is passed as `data`/`size` to the halftone MMR decoder for the first bitplane (GSBPP-1).
jbig2_decode_mmr_init pre-buffers up to 4 input bytes into the 32-bit word buffer (data_index=0, bit_index=0). With a 1-byte payload the remaining 24 bits of the word are initialized zero padding.

Root cause: the refill guard `data_index + 4 < size` fails once the decoder reaches the tail of the segment, so no byte is read from `data`, yet `data_index` is unconditionally incremented. Bits consumed from the 32-bit word buffer (real data plus zero padding) are therefore reported as bytes consumed from the input even though they were never read.

The inflated `mmr.data_index` (plus partial-byte rounding) is propagated as the number of consumed bytes. For the 1-byte PoC payload the line decode consumes 9 bits, so consumed_bytes becomes 2 > size=1.

fine_trace.code: code = jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr(ctx, &rparams, data + consumed_bytes, size - consumed_bytes, GSPLANES[j], &consumed_bytes);
fine_trace.note: Caller subtracts the incorrect consumed_bytes from size for the next bitplane: `size - consumed_bytes` underflows (size_t wraps to a huge value) and `data + consumed_bytes` points past the MMR encoded input buffer.

Sink: the subsequent MMR decoding (bitplane 0) calls jbig2_decode_mmr_init with data+consumed_bytes and the wrapped size, reading 4 bytes from beyond the end of the MMR encoded input buffer (past the end of the file/segment data), i.e. an out-of-bounds/uninitialized read.

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: Matches the issue: the MMR decoder pre-buffers up to 32 bits in a word, reports bytes as consumed without reading them when refilling near the end of the segment, propagates the incorrect consumed-byte count to the caller, and the caller's `size - consumed_bytes` underflows so subsequent MMR decoding reads outside the encoded input buffer.
